A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the insertion of the new IS element, IS1441, in the scaffoldin gene, cipA of C. thermophilum results in a defective cellulosome and a reduction of the specific activity of the cellulosome on crystalline cellulose, which is the most abundant form of cellulose in nature.
the insertion sequence IS1447, a new member of the IS3 family, is inserted into cipA of C. thermophilum, which results in the loss of CipA, the scaffoldin of the cellulosome.
the insertion of IS1447 into cipA leads to a loss of cellulose-binding activity, resulting in a loss of cellulase synergism and, therefore, in a loss of cellulosome function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CipA protein is the scaffold for the assembly of the cellulosome complex, and its absence results in a significant reduction in the ability of the cellulosomes to hydrolyze cellulose.
the insertion sequence IS1447 is a new member of the IS3 family, and it is the first insertion sequence identified in Clostridium.
